thread.title: Spotify Earnings Report Disappoints On Sales

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: Spotify Earnings Report Disappoints On Sales
text:
Streaming music leader Spotify Technology ( SPOT ) on Wednesday swung to a profit in the fourth quarter, beating Wall Street's earnings target. But its average revenue per user continued to fall. The Spotify earnings report sent its stock lower.
X The Stockholm-based company earned 41 cents a share on sales of $1.71 billion in the December quarter. Analysts expected Spotify to lose 22 cents a share on sales of $1.72 billion. In the year-earlier period, it lost $4.56 a share on sales of $1.35 billion.
Spotify stock sank 2.8% to 135.45
Spotify added 8 million paying subscribers to its premium service in the fourth quarter, bringing its total to 96 million worldwide. The company had guided to 93 million to 96 million for the period. On a year-over-year basis, the number of paying subscribers rose 36%. It credited its holiday advertising campaign and a hardware bundle promotion with Alphabet 's ( GOOGL ) Google Home smart speakers for the gain.
 Last week, rival Apple ( AAPL ) reported having more than 50 million subscribers for its Apple Music service.
Spotify Earnings Report Disappoints On User Revenue Premium service revenue accounted for 88% of Spotify's total revenue in the December quarter. Average revenue per user declined 7% year over year in local currency to the equivalent of $5.58. Spotify reports its results in euros.
Spotify attributed the dip in average revenue per user to a greater percentage of users on student and family plans and growth in emerging markets.
Its monthly active users increased 29% year over year to 207 million. That includes users of its advertising-supported free service tier. It had guided to 199 million to 206 million users.
For the March quarter, Spotify expects to reach 97 million to 100 million premium subscribers, up 29% to 33% year over year. It is targeting 117 million to 127 million paying subscribers for the full year.
Spotify expects first-quarter revenue of $1.65 billion, based on the midpoint of its guidance. It did not give a target for earnings per share. Wall Street had predicted Spotify would lose 37 cents a share on sales of $1.68 billion in the current quarter.
Spotify Buying Podcasting Companies In other news, Spotify said Wednesday it has signed deals to acquire two leading players in the podcast marketplace: Anchor and Gimlet Media.
Spotify sees podcasting as a way to differentiate its service and improve its business fundamentals.
"We intend to lean into this strategy in 2019, both to acquire exclusive content and to increase investment in the production of content in-house," the company said in a written statement. It expects to spend $400 million to $500 million on acquisitions in 2019.
